```{r Step 2: Affirmative Action Support Over Time Across Black and White, include=TRUE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function for income × stock models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_income_stock_models <- function(data, outcome) {

  lapply(
    sort(unique(data$year)),
    function(y) {

      data_y <- data %>%
        filter(
          year == y,
          !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
          !is.na(income_group_factor),
          !is.na(stock_owns),
          !is.na(VCF0009z)
        )

      if (nrow(data_y) == 0) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      design_y <- survey::svydesign(
        ids = ~1,
        weights = ~VCF0009z,
        data = data_y
      )

      mod <- survey::svyglm(
        as.formula(
          paste0(
            outcome,
            " ~ income_group_factor * stock_owns"
          )
        ),
        design = design_y
      )

      list(
        year = y,
        model = mod,
        n = nrow(data_y),
        outcome = outcome
      )
    }
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Affirmative action
# ------------------------------------------------------------

black_affirmative_race_models <-
  run_income_stock_models(
    black_anes,
    "affirmative_action"
  )

white_affirmative_race_models <-
  run_income_stock_models(
    white_anes,
    "affirmative_action"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Government services
# ------------------------------------------------------------

black_services_race_models <-
  run_income_stock_models(
    black_anes,
    "government_services"
  )

white_services_race_models <-
  run_income_stock_models(
    white_anes,
    "government_services"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Omnibus income × stock test
# ------------------------------------------------------------

get_income_stock_tests <- function(model_list, race_group) {

  lapply(
    model_list,
    function(x) {

      if (is.null(x)) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      mod <- x$model

      interaction_idx <- grep(
        "^income_group_factor.*:stock_owns$",
        names(coef(mod))
      )

      if (length(interaction_idx) == 0) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      beta <- coef(mod)[interaction_idx]

      V <- vcov(mod)[
        interaction_idx,
        interaction_idx,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

      W <- as.numeric(
        t(beta) %*% solve(V) %*% beta
      )

      q <- length(beta)

      F_stat <- W / q

      df_den <- mod$df.residual

      p_value <- pf(
        F_stat,
        df1 = q,
        df2 = df_den,
        lower.tail = FALSE
      )

      data.frame(
        race = race_group,
        outcome = x$outcome,
        year = x$year,
        n = x$n,
        F = F_stat,
        df_num = q,
        df_den = df_den,
        p.value = p_value
      )
    }
  ) %>%
    bind_rows()
}

race_policy_tests <- bind_rows(

  get_income_stock_tests(
    black_affirmative_race_models,
    "Black"
  ),

  get_income_stock_tests(
    white_affirmative_race_models,
    "White"
  ),

  get_income_stock_tests(
    black_services_race_models,
    "Black"
  ),

  get_income_stock_tests(
    white_services_race_models,
    "White"
  )

) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    year,
    race
  )


race_policy_tests_clean <- race_policy_tests %>%
  mutate(
    result = paste0(
      "F(",
      df_num,
      ", ",
      df_den,
      ") = ",
      round(F, 2),
      ", p = ",
      format.pval(
        p.value,
        digits = 3,
        eps = 0.001
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    outcome,
    race,
    n,
    result
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    outcome,
    race
  )

race_policy_tests_clean
```

```{r Step 3: Retesting the Correlation between Personal Finances and Views of the National Economy, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# Personal finances × income × stock ownership
# Separate models for Black and White respondents
# All ANES waves, 2000–2024
# ============================================================

run_finance_econ_income_stock_models <- function(data, race_group) {

  lapply(
    sort(unique(data$year)),
    function(y) {

      data_y <- data %>%
        filter(
          year == y,
          !is.na(econ_views),
          !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
          !is.na(income_group_factor),
          !is.na(stock_owns),
          !is.na(VCF0009z)
        )

      if (nrow(data_y) == 0) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      design_y <- survey::svydesign(
        ids = ~1,
        weights = ~VCF0009z,
        data = data_y
      )

      mod <- survey::svyglm(
        econ_views ~
          personal_finances_scale_factor *
          income_group_factor *
          stock_owns,
        design = design_y
      )

      list(
        year = y,
        model = mod,
        n = nrow(data_y),
        race = race_group
      )
    }
  )
}

# White respondents

# ============================================================
# Omnibus test of the three-way interaction
# ============================================================

get_finance_econ_threeway_tests <- function(
    model_list,
    race_group) {

  lapply(
    model_list,
    function(x) {

      if (is.null(x)) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      mod <- x$model

      # Identify all three-way interaction terms
      interaction_idx <- grep(
        "^personal_finances_scale_factor.*:income_group_factor.*:stock_owns$",
        names(coef(mod))
      )

      if (length(interaction_idx) == 0) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      beta <- coef(mod)[interaction_idx]

      V <- vcov(mod)[
        interaction_idx,
        interaction_idx,
        drop = FALSE
      ]

      # Wald statistic
      W <- as.numeric(
        t(beta) %*% solve(V) %*% beta
      )

      q <- length(beta)

      F_stat <- W / q

      df_den <- mod$df.residual

      p_value <- pf(
        F_stat,
        df1 = q,
        df2 = df_den,
        lower.tail = FALSE
      )

      data.frame(
        race = race_group,
        year = x$year,
        n = x$n,
        F = F_stat,
        df_num = q,
        df_den = df_den,
        p.value = p_value
      )
    }
  ) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    arrange(year)
}

finance_econ_threeway_tests <- bind_rows(

  get_finance_econ_threeway_tests(
    black_finance_econ_income_stock_models,
    "Black"
  ),

  get_finance_econ_threeway_tests(
    white_finance_econ_income_stock_models,
    "White"
  )

) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    race
  )



finance_econ_threeway_tests_clean <-
  finance_econ_threeway_tests %>%
  mutate(
    result = paste0(
      "F(",
      df_num,
      ", ",
      df_den,
      ") = ",
      round(F, 2),
      ", p = ",
      format.pval(

        digits = 3,
        eps = 0.001
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    race,
    n,
    result
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    race
  )

finance_econ_threeway_tests_clean
#For Black respondents: The economic-perception relationship is highly heterogeneous by income and stock ownership in 2016–2024, while affirmative-action attitudes show a renewed income × stock relationship specifically in 2024. For White respondents, The economic-perception relationship shows substantial heterogeneity through 2016 but not in 2020–2024, while affirmative-action attitudes show significant income × stock interactions in both 2020 and 2024.
```

```{r Step 4: Create Plots for Predicted Values, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# Predictions from the three-way economic-perceptions models
# ============================================================

get_finance_econ_threeway_predictions <- function(
    model_list,
    years = c(2016, 2020, 2024)) {

  lapply(
    model_list,
    function(x) {

      if (is.null(x) || !x$year %in% years) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      # Use only income categories and personal-finance
      # categories actually represented in the model
      income_levels <- levels(
        model.frame(x$model)$income_group_factor
      )

      finance_levels <- levels(
        model.frame(x$model)$personal_finances_scale_factor
      )

      marginaleffects::predictions(
        x$model,
        newdata = marginaleffects::datagrid(
          personal_finances_scale_factor = finance_levels,
          income_group_factor = income_levels,
          stock_owns = c(0, 1)
        )
      ) %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        mutate(
          year = x$year,
          race = x$race,
          stock_group = factor(
            stock_owns,
            levels = c(0, 1),
            labels = c(
              "Non-stock owners",
              "Stock owners"
            )
          )
        )
    }
  ) %>%
    bind_rows()
}


# Black respondents
black_finance_econ_predictions <-
  get_finance_econ_threeway_predictions(
    black_finance_econ_income_stock_models
  )


# White respondents
white_finance_econ_predictions <-
  get_finance_econ_threeway_predictions(
    white_finance_econ_income_stock_models
  )


# Combine
finance_econ_threeway_predictions <- bind_rows(
  black_finance_econ_predictions,
  white_finance_econ_predictions
)

      year %in% c(2020, 2024)
    ),
  aes(
    x = personal_finances_scale_factor,
    y = estimate,
    group = stock_group,
    linetype = stock_group
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_grid(
    race ~ year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Personal financial evaluation",
    y = "Predicted national economic evaluation",
    linetype = NULL,
    title = "Personal financial evaluations and perceptions of the national economy",
    subtitle = "Black and White respondents, 2020–2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```
